cues.zh: 并取得了三项颠覆性的突破，

cues.en: at a small Japanese chemical company named Nishia.
cues.zh: 就职于一家名为 Nishia 的日本小型化工企业。

cues.en: They had recently expanded into the production of semiconductors to be used in the manufacture
cues.zh: 他们当时刚把业务拓展到半导体生产领域，用于制造

cues.en: of red and green LEDs.
cues.zh: 红光和绿光 LED。

cues.en: But by the late 1980s, the semiconductor division was on its last legs.
cues.zh: 但到了 1980 年代末，半导体部门已经奄奄一息。

cues.zh: 他们在一个拥挤的市场中，与实力雄厚得多的老牌企业竞争。

cues.zh: 内部气氛开始变得高度紧张。

cues.en: Everyone knew that LEDs have the potential to replace light bulbs, because light bulbs,
cues.zh: 所有人都知道 LED 有潜力取代白炽灯，因为白炽灯——

cues.en: the universal symbol for a bright idea, are actually terrible at making light.
cues.zh: 这个代表灵光一闪的通用符号，发光效率其实极低。

cues.en: They work by running current through a tungsten filament, which gets so hot it glows.
cues.zh: 它的原理是让电流通过钨丝，使其高温发热并发光。

cues.en: But most of the electromagnetic radiation comes out as infrared heat.
cues.zh: 但大部分电磁辐射都以红外热量的形式散失了。

cues.en: Only a negligible fraction is visible light.
cues.zh: 只有微不足道的一小部分变成了可见光。

cues.en: In contrast, LED stands for light-emitting diode, it's right there in the name.
cues.zh: 相比之下，LED代表发光二极管，名字里就写得很清楚。

cues.en: LEDs primarily create light, so they're far more efficient, and a diode is just a
cues.zh: LED主要产生光，因此效率高得多，而二极管只是一种

cues.en: device with two electrodes, which only allows current to flow in one direction.
cues.zh: 带有两个电极、仅允许电流单向流动的器件。

cues.en: So here's how an LED works.
cues.zh: 那么LED是如何工作的呢。

cues.en: When you have an isolated atom, each electron in that atom occupies a discrete energy level.
cues.zh: 当只有一个孤立的原子时，其中的每个电子都占据着一个离散的能级。

cues.en: You can think of these energy levels like individual seats from a hockey stadium.
cues.zh: 你可以把这些能级想象成冰球馆里的一个个独立座位。

cues.en: And all atoms of the same element, when they are far apart from each other, have identical
cues.zh: 而且同一种元素的所有原子，在彼此相距较远时，

cues.en: available energy levels.
cues.zh: 都拥有完全相同的可用能级。

cues.en: But when you bring multiple atoms together to form a solid, something interesting happens.
cues.zh: 但是当你把多个原子聚集在一起形成固体时，有趣的事情发生了。

cues.en: The outermost electrons now feel the pull not only of their own nucleus, but of all
cues.zh: 最外层的电子现在不仅能感受到自身原子核的吸引力，

cues.en: the other nuclei as well.
cues.zh: 还能感受到所有其他原子核的吸引力。

cues.en: And as a result, their energy levels shift, so instead of being identical, they become
cues.zh: 结果就是，它们的能级发生偏移，不再完全相同，而是变成了

cues.en: a series of closely spaced but separate energy levels, an energy band.
cues.zh: 一系列间距很小却相互独立的分立能级，也就是能带。

cues.en: The highest energy band with electrons in it is known as the valence band, and the next
cues.zh: 有电子填充的最高能带被称为价带，

cues.en: higher energy band is called the conduction band.
cues.zh: 而紧随其后的更高能带则叫作导带。

cues.en: You can think of it like the balcony level.
cues.zh: 你可以把它想象成剧院的楼座。

cues.en: In conductors, the valence band is only partially filled.
cues.zh: 在导体中，价带只是部分被填满。

cues.en: This means, with a little bit of thermal energy, electrons can jump into nearby unfilled seats.
cues.zh: 这意味着，只要有一点点热能，电子就能跳到附近空着的座位上。

cues.en: And if an electric field is applied, they can jump from one unfilled seat to the next
cues.zh: 如果施加电场，它们就能从一个空座跳到下一个，

cues.en: and conduct current through the material.
cues.zh: 从而在材料中传导电流。

cues.en: In insulators, the valence band is full, and the difference in energy between the valence
cues.zh: 而在绝缘体中，价带是全满的，且价带与导带之间的

cues.en: and conduction bands, the band gap, is large.
cues.zh: 能量差，即带隙，非常大。

cues.en: charge.
cues.zh: 电荷。

cues.en: So, when an electric field is applied, no electrons can move, there are no available
cues.zh: 因此，当施加电场时，没有电子能够移动，价带中没有空位

cues.en: seats to move into in the valence band, and the band gap is too big for any electrons
cues.zh: 可供移入，而带隙又太大，

cues.en: to jump into the conduction band.
cues.zh: 电子根本无法跃迁到导带中。

cues.en: Which brings us to semiconductors.
cues.zh: 这就引出了半导体。

cues.en: Semiconductors are similar to insulators, except the band gap is much smaller.
cues.zh: 半导体与绝缘体类似，只是其带隙要小得多。

cues.en: This means, at room temperature, a few electrons will have sufficient energy to jump into the
cues.zh: 这意味着，在室温下，少数电子将拥有足够的能量跃迁到导带中，

cues.en: band, and now they can easily access nearby empty seats and conduct current.
cues.zh: 现在它们可以轻松利用附近的空位来传导电流了。

cues.en: Not only that, the empty seats they left behind in the valence band can also move.
cues.zh: 不仅如此，它们在价带中留下的空位也是可以移动的。

cues.en: Well, really, it's the nearby electrons jumping into those empty seats, but if you
cues.zh: 其实，本质是附近的电子跃迁到了这些空位上，但如果

cues.en: look from afar, it's as though the empty seat or hole is moving, like a positive charge
cues.zh: 从远处看，就好像是空位（即空穴）在移动，如同正电荷

cues.en: in the opposite direction to the electrons in the conduction band.
cues.zh: 沿着与导带中电子相反的方向运动。

cues.en: By themselves, pure semiconductors are not that useful.
cues.zh: 纯半导体本身并没有那么大的用处。

cues.en: To make them way more functional, you have to add impurity atoms into the lattice.
cues.zh: 为了让它们发挥更大作用，你得在晶格中掺入杂质原子。

cues.en: This is known as doping.
cues.zh: 这被称为掺杂。

cues.en: For example, in silicon, you can add a small number of phosphorus atoms.
cues.zh: 比如在硅中，你可以加入少量的磷原子。

cues.en: Phosphorus is similar to silicon, so it easily fits into the lattice, but it brings with
cues.zh: 磷和硅很相似，所以很容易融入晶格，但它会额外

cues.en: it one extra valence electron.
cues.zh: 多带来一个价电子。

cues.en: This electron exists in a donor level just beneath the conduction band.
cues.zh: 这个电子存在于紧挨着导带下方的施主能级中。

cues.en: So with a bit of thermal energy, all these electrons can jump into the conduction band
cues.zh: 因此只需一点热能，所有这些电子就能跃迁到导带中，

cues.en: and conduct current.
cues.zh: 并传导电流。

cues.en: Since most of the charges that can move in this type of semiconductor are electrons, which are negative,
cues.zh: 因为这种半导体中大部分可移动的电荷都是带负电的电子，

cues.en: this sort of semiconductor is called n-type, n for negative.
cues.zh: 所以这种半导体被称为 n 型，n 代表负电（negative）。

cues.en: But I should point out that the semiconductor itself is still neutral.
cues.zh: 但我得指出，半导体本身整体仍然是电中性的。

cues.en: It's just that most of the mobile charge carriers are negative, they are electrons.
cues.zh: 只是大多数可移动载流子带负电，它们是电子。

cues.en: So there is also another type of semiconductor where most of the mobile charge carriers are positive,
cues.zh: 因此还有另一类半导体，其中大多数可移动载流子带正电，

cues.en: and it's called p-type.
cues.zh: 它被称为 p 型半导体。

cues.en: To make p-type silicon, you add a small number of atoms of, say, boron.
cues.zh: 要制备 p 型硅，需要掺入少量的杂质原子，比如硼。

cues.en: Boron fits into the lattice, but brings with it one fewer valence electron than silicon.
cues.zh: 硼会嵌入晶格中，但它比硅少一个价电子。

cues.en: So it creates an empty acceptor level just above the valence band.
cues.zh: 因此它会在价带正上方形成一个空的受主能级。

cues.en: And with a bit of thermal energy, electrons can jump out of the valence band, leaving
cues.zh: 借助一点热能，电子就能跃迁离开价带，

cues.en: behind holes.
cues.zh: 留下空穴。

cues.en: It is these positive holes which are mostly responsible for carrying current in the p-type
cues.zh: 正是这些带正电的空穴，在 p 型

cues.en: semiconductor.
cues.zh: 半导体中主要负责传导电流。

cues.en: Again, the material overall is uncharged, it's just that most of the mobile charge
cues.zh: 同样，材料整体呈电中性，只是大多数可移动

cues.en: carriers are positive holes.
cues.zh: 载流子是带正电的空穴。

cues.en: holes.
cues.zh: 空穴。

cues.en: Where things get interesting is when you put a piece of p-type and n-type together.
cues.zh: 有趣的地方在于，当你把一块P型和N型半导体合在一起时。

cues.en: Without even connecting this to a circuit, some electrons will diffuse from n to p and
cues.zh: 甚至都还没接上电路，部分电子就会从N型扩散到P型，

cues.en: fall into the holes in the p-type.
cues.zh: 并填入P型半导体的空穴中。

cues.en: This makes the p-type a little negatively charged and the n-type a little positively
cues.zh: 这会让P型带上一点负电，而N型带上一点正

cues.en: charged.
cues.zh: 电。

cues.en: So there is now an electric field inside an inert piece of material.
cues.zh: 因此，原本惰性的材料内部现在产生了一个电场。

cues.en: Electrons keep diffusing until the electric field becomes so large it prevents them from
cues.zh: 电子会持续扩散，直到电场变得足够强，阻止它们继续

cues.en: crossing over. And now we have established the depletion region, an area depleted of
cues.zh: 穿过。这时就形成了耗尽区，也就是一个缺乏

cues.en: mobile charge carriers. There are no electrons in the conduction band, and no holes in the
cues.zh: 可移动载流子的区域。导带中没有电子，价带中

cues.en: valence band. If you connect a battery the wrong way to this diode, it simply expands
cues.zh: 也没有空穴。如果给这个二极管反向接上电池，它只会进一步扩大

cues.en: the depletion region until its electric field perfectly opposes that of the battery, and
cues.zh: 耗尽区，直到其内建电场与电池电场完全抵消，

cues.en: no current flows. But if you flip the polarity of the battery, then the depletion region
cues.zh: 这样就不会有电流通过。但如果你调转电池的极性，耗尽区就会

cues.en: When an electron shrinks, the electric field decreases, and electrons can flow from N to
cues.zh: 缩小，电场随之减弱，电子就能从N极流向

cues.en: P. When an electron falls from the conduction band into a hole in the valence band, that
cues.zh: P极。当电子从导带跃迁回落到价带的空穴中时，这部分

cues.en: band gap energy can be emitted as a photon.
cues.zh: 带隙能量就可以以光子的形式发射出来。

cues.en: The energy change of the electron is emitted as light.
cues.zh: 电子跃迁释放的能量会以光的形式发射出来。

cues.en: And this is how a light-emitting diode works.
cues.zh: 这就是发光二极管的工作原理。

cues.en: The size of the band gap determines the color of the light emitted.
cues.zh: 带隙的大小决定了发出光的颜色。

cues.en: In pure silicon, the band gap is only 1.1 electron volts, so the photon released isn't visible, it's infrared light.
cues.zh: 在纯硅中，带隙只有 1.1 电子伏特，所以释放的光子是不可见的红外光。

cues.en: These LEDs are actually used in remote controls like for your TV, and you can capture them on camera.
cues.zh: 这种 LED 实际上用在电视等设备的遥控器上，用摄像头就能拍到。

cues.en: Moving up the spectrum, you can see why the first visible light LEDs were red, and then green, and why blue was so hard.
cues.zh: 沿着光谱往上看，你就会明白为什么最早的可见光 LED 是红色的，然后是绿色的，以及为什么蓝光会这么难做。

cues.en: A photon of blue light requires more energy and therefore a larger band gap.
cues.zh: 一个蓝光光子需要更高的能量，因此也需要更大的带隙。

cues.en: By the 1980s, after hundreds of millions of dollars had been spent hunting for the right
cues.zh: 到了 1980 年代，在花费了数亿美元寻找合适的

cues.en: material, every electronics company had come up empty handed.
cues.zh: 材料之后，所有的电子公司都空手而归。

cues.en: But researchers had at least figured out the first critical requirement, high-quality crystal.
cues.zh: 但研究人员至少弄清了第一个关键要求：高质量的晶体。

cues.en: No matter what material you used for the Blue LED, it required a near-perfect crystal structure.
cues.zh: 无论用什么材料来做蓝光 LED，都需要近乎完美的晶体结构。

cues.en: Any defects in the crystal lattice disrupt the flow of electrons,
cues.zh: 晶格中的任何缺陷都会阻碍电子的流动，

cues.en: so instead of emitting their energy as visible light, it is instead dissipated as heat.
cues.zh: 导致能量无法以可见光的形式释放，反而转化为热量散失掉了。

cues.en: So the first step in Nakamura's proposal to Agawa was to disappear to Florida.
cues.zh: 所以中村向小川提出的第一步建议，就是先“隐身”去佛罗里达。

cues.en: He knew an old colleague there whose lab was beginning to use a new crystal-making technology
cues.zh: 他认识那里的一位老同事，对方的实验室正开始采用一种新的制晶技术，

cues.en: called Metal Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition, or MOCVD.
cues.zh: 也就是金属有机化学气相沉积，简称 MOCVD。

cues.en: An MOCVD reactor, essentially a giant oven, was and still is the best way to mass produce
cues.zh: MOCVD 反应炉本质上就是一个巨大的烤箱，它在当时乃至现在都是量产

cues.en: clean crystal.
cues.zh: 高纯度晶体的最佳途径。

cues.en: It works by injecting vapor molecules of your crystal into a hot chamber, where they react
cues.zh: 它的工作原理是将晶体原料的气态分子注入高温腔室，使其与

cues.en: with a base material called a substrate to form layers.
cues.zh: 被称为衬底的基础材料发生反应，从而形成一层层的薄膜。

cues.en: Nakamura joined the lab for a year to master MOCVD.
cues.zh: Nakamura 加入该实验室进修一年，以掌握 MOCVD 技术。

cues.en: But his time there was miserable.
cues.zh: 但他在那里的日子苦不堪言。

cues.en: He wasn't allowed to use the working MOCVD, so he spent 10 of his 12 months assembling a new system almost from scratch.
cues.zh: 他没被允许使用现成的 MOCVD 设备，于是在12个月里，他花了整整10个月几乎从零组装了一台新系统。

cues.en: Even worse, his lab mates shunned him, because Nakamura didn't have a doctorate, nor any academic papers to his name, as Nishiya didn't allow publishing.
cues.zh: 更糟糕的是，实验室同僚都排挤他，因为 Nakamura 没有博士学位，而且由于 Nishiya 不准发表成果，他名下也没有任何学术论文。

cues.en: His lab mates, all PhD researchers, dismissed him as a lowly technician.
cues.zh: 他的同僚全都是博士研究员，都瞧不起他，把他当成底层技术员。

cues.en: This experience fueled him. Nakamura wrote,
cues.zh: 这段经历激发了他的斗志。Nakamura 写道：

cues.en: I feel resentful when people look down on me. I developed more fighting spirit.
cues.zh: “当别人看不起我时，我会心生愤慨。这反而激起了我更强的斗志。”

cues.en: I would not allow myself to be beaten by such people.
cues.zh: 我绝不容许自己输给那样的人。

cues.en: He returned to Japan in 1989 with two things in hand.
cues.zh: 1989年，他带着两样东西回到了日本。

cues.en: One, an order for a brand new MOCVD reactor for Nishiya, and two, a fervent desire to get his PhD.
cues.zh: 一是给日亚订购的全新 MOCVD 反应炉，二是他拿到博士学位的强烈渴望。

cues.en: At that time in Japan, you could earn a PhD without having to go to university, simply
cues.zh: 当时在日本，你不用去大学上课也能拿到博士学位，只要

cues.en: by publishing five papers.
cues.zh: 发表五篇论文就行。

cues.en: Nakamura had always known his chances of inventing the Blue LED were low, but now he had a backup
cues.zh: Nakamura 一直知道自己研发出蓝光 LED 的几率很小，但现在他有了后备

cues.en: plan.
cues.zh: 方案。

cues.en: Even if he didn't succeed, he could at least get his PhD.
cues.zh: 就算没成功，他起码还能拿到博士学位。

cues.en: But now the question was, with MOCVD under his belt, which material should he research?
cues.zh: 但现在的问题是，掌握了 MOCVD 技术后，他该研究哪种材料呢？

cues.en: By this time, scientists had narrowed the options down to two main candidates, zinc
cues.zh: 到那时，科学家们已经把选项缩小到了两个主要候选者：硒化

cues.en: selenide and gallium nitride. These were both semiconductors with band gaps theoretically in
cues.zh: 锌和氮化镓。这两种半导体的带隙理论上都处于

cues.en: the blue light range. Zinc selenide was the far more promising option. When grown in an
cues.zh: 蓝光范围内。硒化锌在当时是更有前景的选择。在

cues.en: MOCVD reactor, it had only a 0.3% lattice mismatch with its substrate, gallium arsenide.
cues.zh: MOCVD 反应炉中生长时，它与衬底砷化镓的晶格失配率仅有 0.3%。

cues.en: Therefore, zinc selenide crystal had about 1000 defects per square centimeter within the
cues.zh: 因此，硒化锌晶体每平方厘米大约只有1000个缺陷，完全在

cues.en: upper limit for LED functioning.
cues.zh: LED正常工作的上限之内。

cues.en: Its only issue was that while scientists had figured out multiple different ways to create
cues.zh: 它唯一的问题是，尽管科学家已经找到了多种制造

cues.en: n-type zinc selenide, no one knew how to create p-type.
cues.zh: N型硒化锌的方法，但没人知道怎么制造P型。

cues.en: In contrast, gallium nitride had been abandoned by almost everybody for three reasons.
cues.zh: 相比之下，氮化镓几乎被所有人放弃了，原因有三。

cues.en: First, it was much harder to make a high-quality crystal.
cues.zh: 首先，制造高质量晶体的难度要大得多。

cues.en: The best substrate for growing gallium nitride was sapphire, but its lattice mismatch was
cues.zh: 生长氮化镓最好的衬底是蓝宝石，但它的晶格失配率高达

cues.zh: 这导致了更多的缺陷，每平方厘米超过100亿个。

cues.en: The second problem was that, like zinc selenide, scientists had only ever created N-type gallium nitride using silicon.
cues.zh: 第二个问题是，和硒化锌一样，科学家此前只用硅制造出过N型氮化镓。

cues.en: P-type was elusive.
cues.zh: P型依然难以实现。

cues.en: And third, to be commercially viable, a blue LED would have to have a total light output power of at least a thousand microwatts.
cues.zh: 第三，要具备商业可行性，蓝光 LED 的总发光输出功率至少要达到 1000 微瓦。

cues.en: That's two orders of magnitude more than any prototype had ever achieved.
cues.zh: 这比当时任何原型机所达到的水平都要高出两个数量级。

cues.en: So between the two candidates, almost all researchers were focused on zinc selenide.
cues.zh: 所以在两种候选材料中，几乎所有研究人员都集中在硒化锌上。

cues.en: Nakamura surveyed the crowded field and decided that if he were going to publish five papers by
cues.zh: Nakamura 审视了这片拥挤的领域，决定如果自己要独立发表五篇论文，

cues.en: himself, he'd better focus on gallium nitride, where the competition was much less fierce.
cues.zh: 最好还是专注于氮化镓，因为那里的竞争要小得多。

cues.en: This material's main claim to fame was one development back in 1972, when RCA engineer
cues.zh: 这种材料最出名的一项进展还要追溯到 1972 年，当时 RCA 工程师

cues.en: Herbert Marusca made a tiny gallium nitride blue LED, but it was dim and inefficient,
cues.zh: Herbert Marusca 制造了一颗微型氮化镓蓝光 LED，但它亮度低且效率不高，

cues.en: so RCA slashed the project's budget, calling it a dead end.
cues.zh: 于是 RCA 大幅削减了该项目的预算，称其为一条死胡同。

cues.en: Twenty years later, scientific opinion hadn't changed.
cues.zh: 二十年后，学术界的看法依然没有改变。

cues.en: When Nakamura attended the biggest applied physics conference in Japan, the Toxon zinc
cues.zh: 当中村修二参加日本最大的应用物理学会议时，硒化锌

cues.zh: 分会场聚集了 500 多名听众。

cues.en: The Toxon gallium nitride had five.
cues.zh: 而氮化镓分会场只有五个人。

cues.en: Two of those five attendees were the world experts on gallium nitride.
cues.zh: 这五个人中，有两位是全球顶尖的氮化镓专家。

cues.en: Dr. Isumu Akazaki and his former grad student Dr. Hiroshi Amano.
cues.zh: 赤崎勇博士和他昔日的研究生天野浩博士。

cues.en: In contrast to Nakamura's academic background, they were researchers at Nagoya University,
cues.zh: 与中村的学术背景截然不同，他们是名古屋大学的研究人员，

cues.en: one of Japan's best.
cues.zh: 那可是日本顶尖学府之一。

cues.en: A few years earlier, they had made a breakthrough on the first problem of high-quality crystal.
cues.zh: 几年前，他们就在解决高质量晶体这一首要难题上取得了突破。

cues.en: soil.
cues.zh: 基底。

cues.en: Instead of growing gallium nitride directly on the surface of the soil, the soil would
cues.zh: 他们没有直接在基底表面生长氮化镓，基底使用的是

cues.en: sapphire, they first grew a buffer layer of aluminum nitride. This has a lot of spacing
cues.zh: 蓝宝石，而是先在上面生长了一层氮化铝缓冲层。它的晶格间距

cues.en: in between that of the other two materials, making it easier to grow a clean gallium nitride
cues.zh: 介于另外两种材料之间，使得在上面生长出纯净的氮化镓

cues.en: crystal on top. The only issue was that the aluminum caused problems for the MOCVD reactor,
cues.zh: 晶体变得更加容易。唯一的问题是铝会对 MOCVD 反应器造成损害，

cues.en: making the process hard to scale. But Nakamura wasn't even close at this stage.
cues.zh: 导致该工艺难以规模化。但此时的中村，甚至连这一步都还没做到。

cues.en: Back at Nishiya, he couldn't get gallium nitride to even grow normally in his new
cues.zh: 回到日亚后，他甚至无法让氮化镓在他的新

cues.en: MOCVD reactor. After six months, desperate for results, he decided to take the machine
cues.zh: MOCVD反应室中正常生长。六个月后，急于看到成果的他决定把机器

cues.en: apart and build a better version himself. His ten months spent putting together the reactor
cues.zh: 拆开，亲手打造一个更好的版本。他在佛罗里达组装反应室的

cues.en: in Florida were suddenly invaluable. He began following the same routine each day. Arrive
cues.zh: 那十个月，突然变得无比珍贵。他开始日复一日地遵循同样的作息。

cues.en: at the lab at 7am. Spend the first half of the day welding, cutting, and rewiring the reactor.
cues.zh: 早上7点到达实验室。前半天用来对反应室进行焊接、切割和重新布线。

cues.en: Spend the rest of the day experimenting with the modified reactor to see what it can do.
cues.zh: 后半天用改装后的反应室做实验，看看它能做到什么程度。

cues.en: At 7pm, go home, eat dinner, wash, and sleep.
cues.zh: 晚上7点，回家、吃晚饭、洗漱、睡觉。

cues.en: Nakamura repeated this routine every single day, taking no weekends and no holidays except
cues.zh: 中村每天都在重复这样的日常，没有周末，没有假期，除了

cues.en: for New Year's Day, the most important holiday in Japan.
cues.zh: 日本最重要的节日——元旦。

cues.en: After a year and a half of continuous work, he came into the lab on a winter day in
cues.zh: 经过一年半的持续努力，他在1990年底的一个

cues.en: late 1990.
cues.zh: 冬日来到了实验室。

cues.en: As usual, he tinkered around in the morning, grew a gallium nitride sample in the afternoon,
cues.zh: 像往常一样，他上午鼓捣设备，下午生长氮化镓样品，

cues.en: and tested it. But this time, the electron mobility was four times higher
cues.zh: 然后进行测试。但这一次，电子迁移率直接比以往任何

cues.en: than any gallium nitride ever grown directly on sapphire. Nakamura called it
cues.zh: 直接在蓝宝石上生长的氮化镓高出了四倍。Nakamura称这一天为

cues.en: the most exciting day of his life. His trick was to add a second nozzle to the
cues.zh: 他一生中最激动的时刻。他的诀窍是在

cues.en: MOCVD reactor. The gallium nitride reactant gases had been rising in the
cues.zh: MOCVD反应腔中加入了第二个喷嘴。氮化镓反应气体原本会在

cues.en: hot chamber, mixing in the air to form a powdery waste. But the second nozzle
cues.zh: 高温反应腔中上升，并在空气中混合形成粉末状废料。但第二个喷嘴

cues.en: released a downward stream of inert gas, pinning the first flow to the substrate to form a
cues.zh: 向下喷出一股惰性气流，将第一股气流压在衬底上，从而形成了

cues.en: uniform crystal.
cues.zh: 均匀的晶体。

cues.en: For years, scientists had avoided adding a second stream to MOCDD because they thought
cues.zh: 多年来，科学家们一直避免在MOCVD中加入第二股气流，因为他们认为

cues.en: it would only introduce more turbulence, but Nakamura used a special nozzle so that even
cues.zh: 这只会引入更多湍流，但Nakamura采用了一种特殊喷嘴，使得两股气流即便

cues.en: when the streams combined, they remained laminar.
cues.zh: 汇合在一起，也依然能保持层流状态。

cues.en: He called his invention the two-flow reactor.
cues.zh: 他把自己的发明命名为双流反应器。

cues.en: Now, he was ready to take on Akazaki and Amano.
cues.zh: 现在，他准备好向 Akazaki 和 Amano 发起挑战了。

cues.en: But instead of copying their aluminum nitride buffer layer, his two-flow design allowed
cues.zh: 但他没有照搬他们的氮化铝缓冲层，双流反应器的设计让他能

cues.en: him to make gallium nitride so smooth and stable, it itself could be used as a buffer
cues.zh: 制造出极其平整、稳定的氮化镓，可以直接用作

cues.en: layer on the sapphire substrate.
cues.zh: 蓝宝石衬底上的缓冲层。

cues.en: This in turn yielded an even cleaner crystal of gallium nitride on top, without the issues
cues.zh: 这反过来又在表层生长出了更纯净的氮化镓晶体，完全没有铝带来的

cues.en: of aluminum.
cues.zh: 那些问题。

cues.en: Nakamura now had the highest-quality gallium nitride crystals ever made.
cues.zh: Nakamura 此时拥有了有史以来最高品质的氮化镓晶体。

cues.en: But, just as he was getting started, things took a wrong turn.
cues.zh: 然而，正当他准备大展拳脚时，事情却急转直下。

cues.en: While he had been in Florida, Nobuo Ogawa had stepped back from Nishia to become chairman.
cues.zh: 当他还在佛罗里达时，Nobuo Ogawa 就已经退居幕后，转任 Nishia 的董事长。

cues.en: In his day, Nobuo had been a risk-taking scientist, designing the company's first
cues.zh: 在 Nobuo 的时代，他曾是一位敢于冒险的科学家，亲手设计了公司的第一批

cues.en: products.
cues.zh: 产品。

cues.en: It's why he supported Nakamura's lofty plans all this time.
cues.zh: 正因如此，他一直以来都支持 Nakamura 那些宏伟的计划。

cues.en: But in his place, his son-in-law, Eiji Ogawa, became CEO of the company, and the younger
cues.zh: 但在他退位后，他的女婿 Eiji Ogawa 接任了公司 CEO，而年轻的

cues.en: Ogawa had a much stricter outlook.
cues.zh: Ogawa 风格则严苛得多。

cues.en: One Nishiya client said, he has a mind of steel, and he remembers everything.
cues.zh: 一位 Nishiya 的客户曾说，他有着钢铁般的意志，而且过目不忘。

cues.en: In 1990, an executive at Matsushida, an LED manufacturer and Nishiya's biggest customer,
cues.zh: 1990 年，LED 制造商兼 Nishiya 最大客户 Matsushida 的一位高管，

cues.en: visited the company to give a talk on blue LEDs.
cues.zh: 来到公司做了一场关于蓝光 LED 的讲座。

cues.en: In it, he claimed zinc selenide was the way forward, declaring gallium nitride has no
cues.zh: 在演讲中，他断言硒化锌才是未来的方向，并宣称氮化镓根本

cues.en: future.
cues.zh: 没有前途。

cues.en: That very same day, Nakamura received a note from Eiji.
cues.zh: 就在当天，Nakamura 收到了 Eiji 写的一张便签。

cues.en: Stop work on gallium nitride immediately.
cues.zh: 立刻停止氮化镓的研发工作。

cues.en: Eiji had never supported the research and wanted to end what he saw as a colossal waste.
cues.zh: Eiji 从未支持过这项研究，他想彻底终结这场在他看来极其巨大的浪费。

cues.en: But Nakamura crumpled up the note and threw it away.
cues.zh: 但 Nakamura 把便签揉成一团，随手扔掉了。

cues.en: And he did so again and again when a succession of similar notes and phone calls came from company management.
cues.zh: 当公司管理层接二连三发来类似的通知和电话时，他也一次又一次地照做。

cues.en: Out of spite, he published his work on the two-flow reactor without Nishiya's knowledge.
cues.zh: 出于赌气，他在西谷不知情的情况下发表了关于双流反应器的研究成果。

cues.en: It was his first paper.
cues.zh: 那是他的第一篇论文。

cues.en: One down, four to go.
cues.zh: 解决了一个，还剩四个。

cues.en: With crystal formation settled, he turned to the second obstacle, creating p-type gallium
cues.zh: 结晶问题搞定后，他转向了第二个障碍：制造 p 型氮化

cues.en: nitride.
cues.zh: 镓。

cues.en: Here, Akazaki and Amano had again beaten him to the punch.
cues.zh: 在这一点上，赤崎和天野再次抢先了一步。

cues.en: They had created a gallium nitride sample doped with magnesium.
cues.zh: 他们制造出了掺镁的氮化镓样品。

cues.en: But at first, it didn't perform as a p-type as they expected.
cues.zh: 但一开始，它并没有像他们预期的那样呈现出 p 型特性。

cues.en: However, after exposing it to an electron beam, it did behave as a p-type, the world's
cues.zh: 然而，在经过电子束照射后，它确实表现出了 p 型特性，这也是世界上

cues.zh: 历经20年的努力后的首个 p 型氮化镓。

cues.en: The catch was that no one knew why it worked, and the process of irradiating each crystal
cues.zh: 问题在于，没人知道它为什么管用，而且用电子束照射每个晶体的过程

cues.en: with electrons was too slow for commercial production.
cues.zh: 太慢了，无法用于商业化生产。

cues.en: At first, Nakamura copied Akazaki and Amano's approach,
cues.zh: 起初，Nakamura借鉴了Akasaki和Amano的方法，

cues.en: but he suspected the beam of electrons was overkill.
cues.zh: 但他怀疑用电子束可能小题大做了。
